judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short descriptive definition of the MERS system.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the MIN, MOM Loan definitions and Section 2.01's MERS carve-outs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short identifier definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Section 2.01 and the Mortgage Loan Schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tied to the Mortgage Note; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Maximum Mortgage Rate and Periodic Rate Cap definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition defines a loan by describing MERS's role rather than defining the loan itself ('MOM Loan: ... MERS acting as the mortgagee'), a grammatical mismatch between definiendum and definiens.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.01 turns on whether a loan 'is a MOM Loan' for delivery of assignments, so the mismatch has operative consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference to Section 6.06.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.06 is Monthly Statements to Certificateholders; correct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A rating agency name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Rating Agency and Eligible Account definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'creating a first lien on or first priority ownership interest in an estate in fee simple' is a narrow, specific formulation with no catch-all for other collateral positions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Mortgage Loan Schedule definition expressly contemplates 'second lien Mortgage Loan[s]' and CLTV for them, which cannot be reconciled with a Mortgage that must be a first lien.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to the Section 2.01 list plus 'any additional documents delivered ... pursuant to this Agreement', an open-ended tail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02's certification review is expressly limited for subclauses (iv) and (vi) of Section 2.01, so the scope of the Mortgage File matters and the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition deems a loan that was never transferred to remain a Mortgage Loan, a deliberately counterfactual construct that invites argument about what it means.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'the representation contained in Section 2.03(b)(v) hereof', but Section 2.03(b) is only a one-sentence survival clause with no subclause (v), so the cross-reference is broken.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific dated agreement in exhibit form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit L matches the exhibit list; central to Sections 2.01–2.03 and consistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference to Section 11.01.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.01 is the optional termination/repurchase section; correct, though it is easily confused with the separate 'Purchase Price' term used in Sections 2.02–2.03.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated field list contains multiple mechanical errors — two items lettered '(aa)', a garbled '(¢4)', 'the the Periodic Rate Cap', 'whether the Mortgage Loan is has a balloon payment' — and several '[reserved]' gaps.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to second lien Mortgage Loans and CLTV, which conflicts with the Mortgage definition's first-lien requirement, and the closing averaging sentence references items '(h) and (u) through (w)' whose lettering is unreliable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or other evidence of indebtedness' is a small catch-all but the referent is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.01's delivery requirements and the lost-note exception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line rate definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Net Mortgage Rate, Gross Margin and the adjustable-rate definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The underlying property securing a Mortgage Loan' is terse but plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Mortgage and REO Property definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The obligors on a Mortgage Note' — plural definiens for a singular term, a trivial slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout Article IV.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise subtraction of three enumerated rates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Servicing Fee Rate, Master Servicing Fee Rate and LPMI Fee definitions and the Net Rate Cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long two-part formula plus a separate federal-tax version of the same cap; having two different meanings for one defined term is a genuine source of argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Preliminary Statement footnote to the REMIC III table says the Net Rate Cap for each REMIC III Regular Interest 'is specified in the definition of Net Rate Cap', which this definition does address, so the two are reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and determinate, with an express exclusion of Swap Termination Payments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.22(c) and the Net Rate Cap definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in the good faith judgment of the Master Servicer or the related Servicer, will not ... be ultimately recoverable ... or otherwise' is a classic discretionary and open-ended standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It controls reimbursements under the Interest Funds definition and Sections 5.01/5.03, but nothing there contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One term carries three different meanings (certificate, federal tax, swap) in four sentences, which is the sort of layering that generates disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties to the Uncertificated Notional Amount definition and Exhibit M; the initial figure matches the Cut-off Date Principal Balance plus Special Deposit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed enumeration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Book-Entry Certificates definition, which names the Offered Certificates plus Class B-4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: After a long list of named offices it adds 'any other officer customarily performing functions similar to those performed by any of the above designated officers', a catch-all whose reach is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.03(a) lets the Master Servicer rely on a Servicer's Officer's Certificate, so who may sign matters, but no provision contradicts this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed rate-setting cascade with express fallbacks and a 'manifest error' finality clause; unusually complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Interest Determination Date, LIBOR Business Day and LIBOR Certificates definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonably acceptable to each addressee' is a soft standard, and the independence proviso lists particular sections without a general test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names Sections 2.05, 8.05, 8.07 and 12.01 for independent counsel but Section 4.02's REMIC Opinion requirement is not on the list, an expressio unius gap between the definition and that section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference to Section 11.01 with a short description.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Optional Termination Date and Mortgage Loan Purchase Price definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 5% clean-up-call trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Every Pass-Through Rate definition steps up after this date, and Section 11.01 governs the termination itself; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined solely by the Mortgage Loan Schedule entry; determinate but wholly dependent on the schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.02(d) and 2.03 impose repurchase and notice duties on 'the related Originator', so identifying the Originator through the schedule is load-bearing; the schedule definition does list '(ee) the related Seller' but not expressly the originator.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agency name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Delinquent definition's OTS method reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exhaustive definition with two enumerated exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.02 and 7.03 on cancellation and replacement certificates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three cumulative conditions, each objectively determinable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Stated Principal Balance, Liquidated Loan and Prepayment Period definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise excess formula with the Special Deposit added for the first date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Overcollateralization Target and Release Amount definitions and the Enhancement Percentages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lesser-of formula with an explicit deeming rule; complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Excess Cashflow, Principal Funds and Overcollateralization Target Amount.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-branch stepdown formula; each branch is spelled out and the floor figure matches the $3,675,502 used in the Principal Distribution Amount definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Stepdown Date and Trigger Event definitions, which supply the branch conditions; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any ownership interest ... whether direct or indirect, legal or beneficial' is deliberately all-encompassing rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Permitted Transferee definition and the Article VII transfer restrictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence lists 'the Class CE Pass-Through Rate' as an available Pass-Through Rate while the next sentence says the Class CE Certificate has no Pass-Through Rate; the distinction between the Class CE Interest and Certificate rescues it only on a careful reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the Class CE Pass-Through Rate definition and the Preliminary Statement footnotes, which allocate the rate to the Interest rather than the Certificate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line capacity definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Securities Administrator's distribution role in Sections 5.02–5.03 and 6.04.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two alternative methods (face amount or computed fraction) without a rule for which prevails if they diverge; 'the such Class' is a typo.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Denomination definition, whose own quotation is garbled, so the two interlocking definitions are both slightly damaged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise cap definition with an express disregard of the Maximum/Minimum rates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Maximum and Minimum Mortgage Rate definitions and the Mortgage Loan Schedule field.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-item list closing with clause (x), 'such other investments ... acceptable to each Rating Agency', a broad catch-all, and the provisos use undefined terms like 'purchased at a deep discount'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An extremely long tax-driven definition, but each exclusion is tied to a specific Code section; limb (z) turns on an Opinion of Counsel rather than an objective test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with the Ownership Interest definition and the Residual Certificate transfer restrictions; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional exhaustive list of entity types.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The applicable rate of prepayment, as described in the Prospectus Supplement' points wholly outside the instrument and gives no rate on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three near-synonyms ('premium, penalty or charge') tied to the Mortgage Note; broad but bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Prepayment Charge Waiver Amount and Class P Certificate definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites Section 5.01(a) (Master Servicer Account) as the source of the payment, which is plausible, and the amount is excluded from REMIC I in c003; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subtraction is of '(a) the related Servicing Fee, (b) the Master Servicing Fee Rate and (c) the LPMI Fee' — subtracting a rate alongside two fees is a mechanical error that makes the arithmetic incoherent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel Net Mortgage Rate definition subtracts three rates and the Interest Funds definition subtracts three fees, so this hybrid fits neither.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precisely bounded 16th-to-15th window with a first-period carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Runs alongside the Due Period definition; the two windows differ deliberately and the distribution formulas use each expressly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing words 'or any replacement policy therefor through the related Interest Accrual Period for such Class relating to a Distribution Date' are unintelligible in a policy definition and appear to be text imported from elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.11 requires maintenance of the Primary Mortgage Insurance Policies, so the garbled tail affects an operative obligation; it also overlaps with the LPMI Policy definition without a stated relationship.
